sentences.text: possession of the land has been taken and the land infact has been handed over to the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board (KIADB) on 27.06.2007 and the same was allotted to respondent No.4 on 29.06.2007.
The petitioner being one of the owner of the land which was acquired, has filed this writ petition in the year 2019 on the ground that the land has not been utilized by the allottee.

Admittedly, the land was acquired under the provisions of Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 (for short 'the Act') and it is a settled principle of law that the land vests with the Government once the final notification is passed.
2. Section 28(5) of the Act, reads as under:-
NC: 2024:KHC:20906 "28. Acquisition of land.-

(1) xxx (2) xxx (3) xxx (4) xxx (5) On the publication in the official Gazette of the declaration under sub-section (4), the land shall vest absolutely in the State Government free from all encumbrances."
3. The only ground urged in the present writ petition is that the land has not been utilized by the allottee.
If that is the case then Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board can initiate appropriate action against the allottee.
It is not open for the land losers / petitioner to question the land acquisition.
There is no reason assigned for the inordinate delay in filing the writ petition.
The writ petition is liable to be dismissed on the ground of delay and laches also.
4. For the aforementioned reasons, the writ petition is hereby dismissed.
NC: 2024:KHC:20906 5. Pending interlocutory applications, if any, stand disposed of.
